title: Every Picture Tells a Dangerous Story: Memory-Augmented Multi-Agent Jailbreak Attacks on VLMs
abstract: arXiv:2604.12616v2 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: Vision-Language Models (VLMs) expand the attack surface of safety-aligned systems by coupling visual perception with text generation. Existing multimodal jailbreak attacks primarily rely on crafted visual content, adversarial perturbations, or image-specific attack strategies, leaving the potential of reusable visual anchors in benign natural images largely unexplored. To address the problem, we introduce \textbf{MemJack}, a memory-augmented multi-agent framework for automated VLM red-teaming with natural images. MemJack combines visual-anchor discovery, visual-semantic camouflage, response evaluation, reflection-guided repair, and dynamic replanning within a closed-loop attack pipeline. translated_title: 每张图片都讲述危险故事：针对视觉语言模型的记忆增强多智能体越狱攻击
translated_abstract: 视觉语言模型（VLMs）通过将视觉感知与文本生成相结合，扩展了安全对齐系统的攻击面。现有的多模态越狱攻击主要依赖于精心制作的视觉内容、对抗性扰动或特定图像的攻击策略，而良性自然图像中可复用视觉锚点的潜力在很大程度上未被探索。为了解决这一问题，我们引入了\textbf{MemJack}，一个用于自动化VLM红队测试的记忆增强多智能体框架，使用自然图像。MemJack在闭环攻击流水线中结合了视觉锚点发现、视觉语义伪装、响应评估、反思引导修复和动态重新规划。除了攻击生成，MemJack还自动将公共图像转换为攻击锚点，支持构建\textbf{MemJack-Bench}，这是一个包含超过113,000条交互式多模态越狱轨迹的数据集，用于安全评估和防御。
tldr: 本文提出MemJack框架，利用记忆增强多智能体自动将自然图像转化为攻击锚点，实现对视觉语言模型的高效越狱攻击，并构建了大规模基准数据集MemJack-Bench。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes MemJack, a memory-augmented multi-agent framework that automatically transforms natural images into attack anchors for efficient jailbreak attacks on VLMs, and constructs a large-scale benchmark dataset MemJack-Bench.
